DbHeader.doc: The 100-byte SQLite database header at file offset 0. Fixed layout per sqlite.org/fileformat2.html. Readers MUST validate magic + reserved zeros; downstream cannot trust a corrupted header. All multibyte integers are big-endian on disk.

PageHeader.doc: B-tree page header. Leaf pages (0x0A index-leaf, 0x0D table-leaf) have 8 bytes; interior pages (0x02 index-interior, 0x05 table-interior) have 12 bytes including a trailing right_child pointer. The conditional 'right_child' field uses the schema's 'when' gate — present iff page_type ∈ {0x02, 0x05}.

right_child.doc: Rightmost child page pointer on interior pages. Absent on leaf pages.

CellPointerArray.doc: The array of cell pointers that immediately follows a PageHeader. Each pointer is a u16_be byte-offset (within the page) at which a cell payload begins. The array length equals the enclosing PageHeader.cell_count — so this type is declared as `list_sized_by` against a sibling count field at its use-site.

CellPayload.doc: A table-leaf cell payload. The record header + body layout is SQLite's 'serial type sequence' framing: a header_length varint, then N varint type tags where each tag encodes BOTH the type (Null/Int*/Real/Blob/Text) AND, for variable-width kinds, the byte-length of the body. The discriminator-encodes-length pattern doesn't decompose into the shape grammar's primitives, so it's declared as a named codec that each target implements in-mapping.
